scenes.title: Transformer Architecture
scenes.narration: In twenty seventeen, a paper titled Attention Is All You Need replaced recurrence with a single idea: let every token look at every other token, all at once. That idea is the transformer, and it underpins nearly every modern language model.

scenes.title: Self-Attention
scenes.narration: Each token is projected into three vectors: a query, a key, and a value. Comparing one token's query against every key produces attention weights, and those weights blend the values together. The result is a representation of each word that already carries the context around it.

bullets: Every token becomes a query, a key, and a value
Query times key scores how much two tokens relate
Softmax turns those scores into attention weights
The output is a context-weighted blend of values

scenes.title: One Layer, Step by Step
scenes.narration: A transformer block is a short, repeated pipeline. Tokens are embedded and given positional information, passed through multi-head attention, normalised, sent through a feed-forward network, and normalised again. Residual connections carry the original signal around each sublayer.

steps: Embed tokens and add positional encoding

scenes.title: Why It Replaced Recurrence
scenes.narration: Recurrent networks read a sentence one step at a time, so training cannot be parallelised and distant words are easily forgotten. Attention compares all positions simultaneously, which fits modern hardware and keeps long-range dependencies just one hop apart.

left.label: RNN / LSTM
points: Sequential: step t waits for step t-1
Hard to parallelise across a sequence

right.label: Transformer
points: All positions attended to in parallel
Any two tokens are one hop apart
Maps cleanly onto GPU matrix maths

scenes.title: The Cost of Attention
scenes.narration: Attention's power has a price. Because every token attends to every other token, compute grows with the square of the sequence length. Doubling the context roughly quadruples the work, which is why efficient attention variants are an active area of research.

scenes.title: Key Takeaways
scenes.narration: Remember three things. Attention lets every token consult every other token directly. Stacking identical blocks, with residuals and normalisation, is what makes the model deep and trainable. And the quadratic cost of attention is the central trade-off you are always designing around.

bullets: Attention connects every token to every other token
Identical blocks stack into depth via residuals
Cost grows quadratically with sequence length
